summary: This week brought structural changes to how the federal government handles UAP investigations, with the establishment of a new interagency governance board and a science advisory council tasked with resolving what officials are calling "the UAP mystery." The Pentagon released its third batch of files under the PURSUE program, which also revealed that China and Russia may have retrieved unidentified objects, adding geopolitical weight to disclosure efforts. Meanwhile, a public forum is being planned to let lawmakers and whistleblowers speak directly to citizens about disclosure, though discussions about panel composition suggest some tension over how skepticism should be represented in these conversations. On the historical front, ongoing scrutiny of the Majestic 12 papers and claims about Vatican archives underscores broader questions about what records actually exist and which agencies are genuinely cooperating with declassification efforts. Congress has set a June 30 deadline for UAP briefings as part of the FY2026 National Defense Authorization Act, keeping pressure on the Pentagon to deliver answers.
